extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners working on automated evaluation and reward-modeling for creative writing (LLM/ML community)
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, curating, and evaluating a benchmark and training data for automated verification of short creative fiction (pairwise comparisons) and training/evaluating LLM-based judges and reward models to match human preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Vivid descriptions and sensory details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a comparison dimension in the 'Writer-ly Criteria' and 'Alternative Criteria' prompts; judges should assess sensory language and the vividness of description when comparing two responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tension
rubrics_metrics.description: Dramatic interest and conflict that sustain reader engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in 'Writer-ly Criteria' as a key dimension; look for elements that create stakes, conflict, or suspense that propel the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern (structural elements and composition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Structural elements and composition of the piece (pattern).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From 'Writer-ly Criteria' — evaluates organization, structural devices, and compositional choices that shape the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy (engaging style and dynamic writing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging style and dynamic writing that maintain reader interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From 'Writer-ly Criteria' — assess voice, pacing, and stylistic vitality; rewards pieces that feel active and compelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insight (meaningful ideas and depth)
rubrics_metrics.description: Meaningful ideas, thematic depth, and insight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From 'Writer-ly Criteria' — evaluate whether a piece provides depth, interesting perspectives, or intellectually/emotionally resonant ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: Unique concepts and unexpected elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears in multiple prompt templates (Alternative Criteria, Reddit-Verbose) — judge novelty and surprise; unexpected twists and fresh concepts are rewarded as often responsible for 'winning' samples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional impact / Emotional resonance
rubrics_metrics.description: How the writing affects the reader emotionally; emotional resonance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed in Alternative Criteria and Reddit-Verbose prompts; preferred stories often contain emotional qualities — lack of emotional impact is a common reason for losing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence (logical flow and narrative structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Logical flow and narrative structure; absence of confusing narrative shifts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From Alternative Criteria and qualitative analysis — anti-patterns include confusing narratives, rapidly shifting point-of-view, or too many underdeveloped characters that impede comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical skill / Writing quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Grammar, diction, style, and polished language use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in Alternative Criteria and Reddit-Verbose lists; grammatical errors and poor diction can contribute to losing samples, though they are not always the primary factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise and satisfaction (twists / satisfying conclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clever twists, satisfying or surprising conclusions that subvert expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited in qualitative analysis of winning samples (unexpected twist, clever punchlines) and in Reddit-Verbose prompts as a dimension for popularity and preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative engagement / Storytelling captivation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether storytelling is captivating and immersive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears in Reddit-Verbose and prompt optimization criteria — judge the ability to engross readers via pacing, voice, and scene construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot discussion importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which discussion of the plot in explanation text correlates with verdict accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical finding: discussions of the plot are most predictive of correctness, correlated with a +14.8% higher correctness among all models; therefore judges/verifiers emphasizing plot may be more aligned with human preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reddit-popularity criteria (community upvote predictors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Aspects that predict Reddit upvotes: originality, engaging narrative style and pacing, emotional impact, clever twists, and technical quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used specifically for the 'predict which will get more upvotes' judge task (Reddit prompts); models asked to predict community preference should weigh these community-specific signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum engagement filter (upvote threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filter out stories with fewer than 10 up-votes to reduce noise from low-engagement posts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality-control preprocessing step: guarantees each story has reasonable engagement; note chosen stories end up with minimum upvote of 14 after other pruning steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Token length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude stories with greater than 2048 tokens to remove excessively long stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality-control preprocessing to keep dataset within a manageable and genre-appropriate length range; referenced as consistent with prior work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum word count
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove entries with fewer than 50 words because they are not sufficiently long to reflect short-story genre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality-control heuristic: very short pieces are excluded as they don't reflect creative fiction expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upvote-difference pairing rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclude pairs with an upvote difference less than 25% to avoid marginal/unreliable preference signals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures that created pairs reflect stronger community preference signals rather than marginal noise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal pairing rule (mitigate exposure bias)
rubrics_metrics.description: Only create pairs where the higher-upvote (chosen) story is published later, mitigating temporal bias from varying exposure durations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows Ethayarajh et al. methodology to reduce confounding from differing time-on-platform; important for attributing preference to story quality rather than exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length-bias mitigation via histogram pruning
rubrics_metrics.description: Prune pairs using a histogram of length differences until achieving symmetry so chosen stories are sometimes shorter and sometimes longer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses observed length bias (65.25% chosen responses were longer) while preserving length diversity; prevents reward models from learning an exploitable length heuristic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position-bias mitigation for LLM judges
rubrics_metrics.description: Randomly shuffle story positions (A/B) and average performance across permutations to account for position bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applied at test time for LLM-as-judge evaluations; reduces spurious favoritism for option position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require explanations before verdict
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruct judges to form explanations prior to verdict generation (Reasoning line then Preferred).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of prompt design: request 'Reasoning: [brief comparison]' followed by 'Preferred: [A or B]'; used to encourage more deliberative judgments and enable analysis of explanation features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardized output format for judges
rubrics_metrics.description: Require strict output formats (JSON for large instruction-tuned models, plaintext for smaller models) to ensure parsable responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt-optimization protocol includes standardizing output format depending on model family/capacity to follow instructions; required for automated evaluation parsing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt-template optimization
rubrics_metrics.description: Hand-construct multiple prompt templates, validate on a midrange model/validation set, and select the template with highest accuracy for the model family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategy used instead of automated prompt-differentiation tools; found automated prompt-optimization libraries produced poorer prompt performance in their experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bradley–Terry discriminative reward objective
rubrics_metrics.description: Train discriminative reward models using Bradley–Terry formulation where each sample is scored and loss is LBT = −log σ(rchosen − rrejected); accuracy is percent where rchosen > rrejected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation guidance: append linear layer to base model's last hidden state and fine-tune all weights; accuracy computed as proportion of correctly ordered pairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generative reward model (GenRM) variants
rubrics_metrics.description: GenRM: treat classification as autoregressive generation predicting which token (A or B) will be selected; GenRM-CoT: include chain-of-thought reasoning preceding prediction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two GenRM variants trained; empirical finding: adding distilled chain-of-thought (CoT) degrades performance for creative-writing verification, likely introducing textual noise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metric: human-agreement accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure verifier/judge performance as agreement with human preferences (percentage of cases matching human-chosen story).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary reported metric across LLM-judges and trained reward models (e.g., best BT models achieve ~78% agreement; Claude-3.7-Sonnet reaches 73%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Test/train temporal split for zero-shot assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct test set from posts after January 2, 2023 and training data from before 2023 to ensure no overlap and enable true zero-shot evaluation for models with earlier cutoffs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data-sourcing rule to prevent contamination of test examples in model pretraining and to enable fair zero-shot assessment of off-the-shelf LLM judges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data-source and licensing transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Release test-set Reddit IDs and use MIT-licensed training repo; acknowledge Reddit user copyrights and follow API terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical requirement for dataset sharing: provide rehydration code, note licensing of source datasets, and document contact with platform (Reddit) regarding API use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical failure modes / qualitative anti-patterns
rubrics_metrics.description: Common characteristics of losing samples: dryness, lack of emotional qualities, confusing narratives, strange diction, too many characters, rapidly shifting POV; occasional grammatical errors and incoherence are present but not the dominant factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these anti-patterns to inform annotation, filtering, and model diagnostics; they highlight aspects where verifiers and generators should improve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of reward-hacking and dataset biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference-based reward models can be exploited by spurious signals (e.g., length bias) and must be trained on carefully filtered datasets to avoid learning shortcuts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper demonstrates that naïve timestamp/upvote pairing or unfiltered data produces length-biased or lower-performing verifiers; careful filtering and balancing are required to produce reliable reward models.
